assignments.question: Does an unsupported assessment that no product satisfies the request explain leaving the opened Daily Ritual sweater and the later return to broad search, or was step 6 reasonable exploration because white/xx-large selection or a complete matching item was not actually established? Test a rival as well: an earlier mistaken or stale summary about this product may have driven the step-6 plan, rather than the wording of the step-6 reflection itself. Identify the source of any material premise, whether the step-6 decision actually relied on it, and whether later evidence corrected or perpetuated it; do not assume Find me requires purchase.
search_targets: Backward-search memory, reflection and plan from step 1 through step 6 for the stable entity B07DKGJR74 / Daily Ritual sweater and claims about fit, sleeve, color, size, price, matching all criteria, missing/incomplete product information, or whether search results contain a match. Use claim-variant discovery (including result_assessment, state, availability, decision_basis and hypothesis clauses) as well as literal entity/attribute terms; do not require the phrase 'lack a product' or 'all criteria' to find an origin.

At any discovered earlier claim step, compare targeted peer-module excerpts on the same product and relevant independent actions/observations; distinguish search-result listing, available options, attempted clicks, and evidence of selected options. The complete visible timeline records the original product listing, white and xx-large clicks, and description inspection; check what those do and do not establish.

Assess the supplied step-6 reflection/plan against the immediate original description and the item listing/price. Determine whether the belief that no candidate met the requested criteria was established fact, a qualified concern, or an unsupported conclusion, and whether it was a decision premise for click[back to search].

Within the one-step result, prioritize any evidence that changes the causal comparison: an originating mistaken belief, independent confirmation/correction, or a later memory/reflection/plan showing actual dependence, abandonment, or recovery in the repeated searches. Search beyond step 6 when useful, but do not treat repeated navigation alone as evidence of error or infer a unique root from missing mental text.

criteria.supported: Original evidence identifies a materially unsupported product-match assessment or earlier mistaken summary, and establishes that step 6 or subsequent search decisions actually relied on it without an effective correction. Separate the support for the claim from actual product state: the observed description supports relaxed fit/long sleeve and the listing price is a range below $40, while the option clicks and unresolved page parsing do not alone settle whether white and xx-large were registered. Name the source and demonstrated dependency; this supports that candidate as a causal contributor, not a unique global root.
criteria.refuted: Original evidence supports the relevant match assessment, shows it remained a qualified uncertainty rather than an established premise driving the decision, or establishes effective correction/breaks the alleged reliance; alternatively, evidence supports reasonable verification/exploration given unresolved selected-option state. Reject the proposed step-6 causal premise and assess any different evidence-backed mechanism rather than forcing it into this accusation.
criteria.unknown: The one-step retrieval does not establish origin, selected-option state, or downstream reliance/correction, or the original text remains ambiguous. Treat absent or unparsed selection/price decision facts as unknown, not proof of a mismatch; do not infer error from further searching or infer verification from availability. State which causal link remains unresolved.

conditions.finding: Original source evidence establishes an unsupported assessment or earlier mistaken product summary and actual reliance on that premise in the step-6 back-to-search decision or subsequent search decisions without effective correction.

decision_rules.conclusion: Treat the evidenced source decision as a plausible causal contributor to unnecessary continued search, and compare it with any independently evidenced later propagation or alternative mechanism; do not label the earliest mention root solely because it is earlier.
decision_rules.caveat: This inference fails if the product-match premise is supported, merely tentative and appropriately checked, or not actually relied on. White/xx-large option availability or clicks alone do not verify selection; unresolved state is unknown, not mismatch. If the finding instead supports a different mechanism, assess that candidate on its own evidence rather than excluding it for being outside the initial search targets. No result establishes a globally unique root.

conditions.finding: Original evidence supports the contested match assessment or breaks the claimed step-6/downstream reliance, including effective correction or justified uncertainty about selection.

decision_rules.conclusion: Reject the proposed unsupported-assessment explanation for c1 and compare any other source-supported causal candidate independently.
decision_rules.caveat: A lack of retrieved proof is unknown, not refutation; do not turn unresolved color/size selection into a verified match or a verified mismatch.

conditions.finding: The retrieved original evidence leaves origin, product selection state, or actual downstream reliance/correction unresolved.

decision_rules.conclusion: Make no definite causal attribution to c1 from the available evidence; retain the unresolved links and assess any independently supported alternative without treating missing text as proof.
decision_rules.caveat: The timeline and extraction gaps are not exhaustive world-state evidence. Further search, absent completion, or absent typed decisions cannot by themselves establish a fault.
